title: Sydney Property Market Data, Trends and Forecasts 2025
paragraphs: The Sydney property market has proved to be incredibly resilient over recent years. After a historic period of growth over the 2021 property boom that saw median values shoot up +25.3 per cent in just 12 months, Sydney house prices corrected at a sharp rate, according toCoreLogic data. 2023 saw a sudden and unexpected turnaround, though, as home values returned to near-peak levels. The pace of growth slowed significantly towards the end of 2024, butSydney is once again on the rise in 2025.

Rising interest rateswere the leading driver of the correction phase in a city where affordability has been stretched to the limit, so it makes sense that, now that rates are falling in 2025, Sydney is seeing a resurgence in growth. Buyers are able to borrow more and increase their budgets, pushing home values higher as a result.

The 2021 property boom sawSydney house pricessurge to record highs before reaching their peak early in 2022. Detached housing lost significant value rapidly since that point, but surprisingly strong and consistent growth returned over 2023. Gains eased back in 2024, though, until a sudden reversal in early 2025.

The median house price in Sydney got another +0.4 per cent boost in May, cementing a consistent upward trend that's still left quarterly gains in positive territory of +1.3 per cent. Annual price changes remain positive at +1.6 per cent and may continue to increase as last year's declines fall away.

Sydney's median house price is still incredibly high, so affordability is hard to come by for first home buyers. Here are some of our top picks for Sydney suburbs where you can buy well below the median house price.

Things wound down somewhat in 2024 but units have been back on the rise in 2025.

Sydney's median unit price notched up by +0.5 per cent in May to just under $860,000. On a quarterly basis, that brings movement to +0.3 per cent, while annual change is closer to flat at -0.2 per cent. Bolstered demand for units due to rising immigration, renewed investor interest and fresh activity from first home buyers priced out of the house market or the extremely tight rental market helped to drive growth throughout 2023 and 2024.

2025 has already seen a sudden reversal to Sydney's property price declines of the previous year, bringing solid growth back to the Harbour City. So what are the big banks saying about what to expect as we move towards the second half of the year?
NAB's latest Sydney house price forecastnow has Sydney dwellings pushing up by just +2.7 per cent in 2025.
Westpac's Sydney real estate forecastnow sees similarly steady growth for 2025 at +3.0 per cent.
Whether or not this growth can be achieved still largely depends on the supply and demand dynamic over the rest of the year, along with the RBA's future interest rate decisions.
Sydney house prices outperformed units throughout the rebound but units and more affordable houses could be well-placed to deliver stronger gains throughout 2025.
Despite more homes being listed for sale and rising prices making property less affordable, the Sydney property market is expected to keep steaming ahead in and well in 2025.
